children.label: When something the dog values follows a behaviour, making that behaviour more likely to happen again.
children.value: When something the dog values follows a behaviour, making that behaviour more likely to happen again.

children.label: In behavioural science, “positive” means something is added, not that it is morally good. Positive reinforcement means adding a valued consequence after a behaviour. Over time, that behaviour tends to appear more often in similar situations. It is different from negative reinforcement, which involves removing something to change behaviour.
children.value: In behavioural science, “positive” means something is added, not that it is morally good. Positive reinforcement means adding a valued consequence after a behaviour. Over time, that behaviour tends to appear more often in similar situations. It is different from negative reinforcement, which involves removing something to change behaviour.

children.label: Your dog sits, you give them a treat they enjoy, and sitting becomes more likely next time you practise in a similar place.
children.value: Your dog sits, you give them a treat they enjoy, and sitting becomes more likely next time you practise in a similar place.

children.label: “Positive” here does not simply mean “nice”, and “negative” does not simply mean “bad”. They describe adding or removing something.
